t: LeetCode 2212 - Maximum Points in an Archery Competition: Subset Search Over 12 Scoring Sections
o: **Understanding the problem.** Bob fires exactly numArrows arrows after Alice, whose per-section counts are fixed in aliceArrows. On section k Bob scores k only by strictly outshooting Alice - ties go to Alice - so winning it costs precisely aliceArrows[k] + 1 arrows (just 1 arrow if Alice shot none). Anything else is wasted, so the task reduces to choosing a subset of the 12 sections whose costs fit the arrow budget while maximizing the sum of their indices. In Example 2 (numArrows = 3, aliceArrows = [0,0,1,0,...,2]) contesting sections 8, 9 and 10 with one arrow each earns 27; grabbing section 11 would consume all 3 arrows for a lone 11 points. With only 2^12 = 4096 subsets, exhaustive enumeration is instant - no cleverness required.
k: Winning section k costs exactly aliceArrows[k] + 1 arrows because ties favor Alice; shooting more there is pure waste.
The problem is a 12-item knapsack: maximize sum of chosen section indices subject to total cost <= numArrows.
Leftover arrows are dumped on section 0 (worth zero) so the output sums to numArrows as required.

a.i: Recurse over sections 0..11 deciding for each whether Bob contests it (paying aliceArrows[i] + 1 arrows and gaining i points) or skips it. Track the best score and the mask of choices that achieved it. Pruning is unnecessary at this size, though the recursion naturally avoids impossible branches by only descending into affordable takes.
s: DFS(i, arrowsLeft, score, mask): at i = 12 record score/mask if improved.
Take branch (only if arrowsLeft >= aliceArrows[i] + 1): subtract cost, add i points, set bit i.
After the search, expand the winning mask into bobArrows with cost aliceArrows[i] + 1 per taken bit.
Dump all unused arrows onto section 0 and return.
a.t: O(2^m) for m = 12 sections - each section branches into take or skip
a.sp: O(m) - recursion depth plus the output array

a.i: Every plan is a 12-bit number; iterate all 4096 masks, tally each mask's arrow cost and point value in one pass over its bits, and keep the highest-scoring affordable mask. Same exponential class as backtracking but branch-free, cache-friendly, and trivially parallelizable - often the cleaner thing to write under pressure.
s: For each mask in 0..4095, sum cost = aliceArrows[i] + 1 and value = i over set bits.
Track the mask with maximal value whose cost fits numArrows.
Expand the winning mask into bobArrows.
a.t: O(2^m * m) - 4096 masks, 12 bits tallied per mask

w: Either exhaustive method is acceptable; mention the O(m * numArrows) knapsack DP as the scalable generalization if the section count grew beyond ~20. Pitfalls: the tie rule demands aliceArrows[k] + 1 arrows, not aliceArrows[k]; forgetting to spend leftover arrows (the judge expects sum(bobArrows) == numArrows); and contesting an unaffordable high section when spreading singles across cheap ones scores more. Any maximal-scoring bobArrows is accepted, so dumping extras on index 0 is safe. Follow-ups: hit an exact target score with minimum arrows, or handle weighted section values (same enumeration with value = weight).
